If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is trending down, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is above true path, subtract 0.5–1.5% for late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen overcorrection.  
When sentiment spikes from negative to positive, shift forecast downward by 1–2% in the first 5 days to reflect sentiment reversal lag.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day for late horizon to prevent runaway bullishness.  
If true price dips below 70% of historical mean within 7 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for early horizon if sentiment remains positive.
